subject: Recount of service availability window & request for credit ruling
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@oakhill.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 22:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden 503 spike during checkout window (NOV10)

Jonas —

We observed a sustained spike of 503s between 2026-11-10T19:12:00Z and 2026-11-10T19:41:00Z on our EU tenant. This impacted checkout throughput (roughly 18k requests/min -> about 60% failure for that 29-min window). Engineering pulled traces and we attached a small bundle; we also exported transaction ids for a subset.

We need confirmation of the service availability window from Redwood, how you are counting the outage window against SLA, and whether Oakhill is eligible for a service credit under section 4.2 of the contract. We are preparing an executive summary for our CRO and procurement and need an initial ruling today if possible.

I've attached the trace bundle (oakhill-raw-traces-20261110.zip). Let me know if you need anything else immediately.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure
Oakhill Commerce

---
Attachment: oakhill-raw-traces-20261110.zip (logs, zipped)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@oakhill.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden 503 spike during checkout window (NOV10)

Marta —

Thanks for the traces and the heads up. We're pulling timeline and telemetry now. Preliminary notes from runtime: we see an increased prefetch/KV eviction rate coincident with a routing fallback into a lower-capacity pool at 19:10Z; that triggered degraded throughput for affected requests.

Next steps from our side:
- David will pull the raw API routing logs and confirm the exact onset and recovery times (expected by 10:30Z).
- Laura will check the SLA counting rules against the Oakhill contract (section you referenced) and the regional availability calculation.

We will treat this as an SLA claim and return an initial availability window and whether the contract entitles Oakhill to a prorated credit. I will request a postmortem and share the invite once we have a confirmed window.

Apologies for the impact — we know checkout is high priority.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment referenced: contract_SLA_section_Oakhill.pdf (contract excerpt)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@oakhill.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden 503 spike during checkout window (NOV10)

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick triage. Two asks from our side while you validate:
1) Please confirm whether the fallback to the lower-capacity pool was customer-visible routing (i.e., unhandled by graceful degradation) or an internal capacity-shift that should be excluded under the SLA carve-outs.
2) If eligible, we will need a written credit amount and the mechanism (account credit vs invoice adjustment) — procurement needs that to reconcile monthly spend.

We can join a quick 20-minute sync if that helps. Our payments team will be in the 12:00–13:00Z window for an update.

—Marta

On a practical note, we flagged related transactions to help scope revenue exposure; I'll share the list via the Drive link if you need it for impacted-transaction accounting.

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@oakhill.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Re: sudden 503 spike during checkout window (NOV10) — request for ruling & postmortem

Laura / David — forwarding Oakhill's ask. Summary of what we need to deliver by EOD:
- A precise availability window (UTC) for the impacted period with a short rationale (routing fallback + KV eviction correlation) that we can quote to Oakhill.
- A determination of SLA entitlement per contract (section 4.2) and the proposed remedy (calculated prorated credit or invoice adjustment). Include the credit calculation and the accounting code.
- A postmortem invite (30–45 min) and an ETA for the full RCA (timeline: initial postmortem note in 48 hours; detailed RCA in 7 business days).

David — can you attach the raw routing log excerpt and a 1–2 sentence note on whether the fallback was customer-visible (i.e., a hard 503 routing decision) or an internal mitigation that resulted in degraded responses?

Laura — please confirm whether any contract carve-outs (maintenance windows, scheduled scaling events, customer misconfiguration) apply; Oakhill disputes that this was induced by anything on their side.

I'll coordinate the postmortem invite and include legal if we think the remedy will be >$25k. Marta — we'll propose a 12:30Z quick sync; I will include David and Laura.

Thanks —
Jonas
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
